title: An agent's bounded tool loop
subtitle: Invented steps and estimated token counts — no AI calls
intro: The agent retrieves context, drafts an answer and checks whether it can finish. It may use a tool at most twice before handing the question to a person.
ask: Are the tool limit, stops and token assumptions clear?
afterwards: The agent will use your feedback to improve the explanation. This offline page calls no model, tool or provider.

items.title: Retrieved context helps the model draft an answer
items.body: Retrieval returns invented reference material. The model drafts a candidate answer; the guardrail is a separate check, not a promise that the model is correct.

items.title: The loop has an explicit two-call tool budget
items.body: A counter starts at zero. Each tool call consumes one of two allowed calls, then returns its result to the model. A rejected answer, exhausted budget or tool error goes to a person. This graph shows an exit path; it does not execute or prove a production loop terminates.

items.title: Both final outcomes say why and what happens next
items.body: A satisfactory checked answer is shown to the person. A handoff pauses automation and asks a person to decide the next action; no automatic retry follows that stop.

items.title: The token chart is an illustrative estimate, not measured billing
items.body: The three disjoint buckets are input/context (1000), model output (300) and tool-result input (100): 1400 total for an invented run. No subtotal is counted twice. Arithmetic is checked, but completeness, provenance and actual provider usage are not.

diagrams.title: At most two tool calls, then answer or handoff

stop.reason: The candidate passed the illustrated check.
stop.next: Show the answer to the person.

stop.reason: The check rejected the answer, the tool failed or the two-call budget ran out.
stop.next: Pause automation. A person reviews the context and chooses the next action.
